key_insight: GaussiAnimate (Skelebones) turns temporally-consistent deformable Gaussian reconstructions into an intuitive, kinematic rig by compressing Gaussians into free-form bones, extracting a mean-curvature skeleton, and skinning the surface — enabling controllable animation of category-level non-rigid objects.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between dense, deformable volumetric representations (Gaussians) that capture fine non-rigid motion and the need for an explicit, temporally-stable kinematic structure for intuitive control and animation.
method: Bones: compress temporally-consistent deformable Gaussians into free-form bones that approximate surface deformations while preserving dynamics.
Skeleton: extract and temporally refine a Mean Curvature Skeleton from canonical Gaussians to produce a stable kinematic backbone.
Skin: scaffold-skin rigging that binds remaining Gaussians/surface to the skeleton, producing an animatable rig with controllable levels of dynamics.
impact: Provides a practical pipeline to convert neural volumetric reconstructions into usable, controllable rigs — making category-level 3D reconstructions directly useful for animation, editing, and downstream ML tasks that require interpretable kinematics.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: Gaussians -> bone compression -> mean-curvature skeleton -> skinning/rig
Before/after frames: raw Gaussian volume vs. surface with overlaid free-form bones and skeleton

paper_title: GaussiAnimate: Reconstruct and Rig Animatable Categories with Level of Dynamics
paper_authors: Jiaxin Wang, Dongxin Lyu, Zeyu Cai, Zhiyang Dou, Cheng Lin
